title: The ticfac pins sit at the top of the staged Dockerfile and bust the whole image cache
description:
SetSandboxTicfacPins inserts ARG TICFAC_VERSION and ARG TICFAC_SHA256_* into the version block at the TOP of the staged Dockerfile. Docker invalidates every layer after a changed instruction, so any ticfac change rebuilds Go, Node, Bun, uv, mise and the rest from scratch - about twenty minutes - when the only thing that actually changed is a 15 MB COPY at the very end.

Pre-existing from prs; found while implementing hn0, where the rebuild cost is paid on every iteration.

Fix: move the ticfac ARG block DOWN beside the COPY that uses it. The pins are still pinned and a rebuild is still a diff of one block; the block just does not need to sit where it poisons every layer below it. Check TARGETARCH's bare re-declaration stays in the same stage as the COPY when it moves.

Worth measuring after: a ticfac-only change should rebuild in seconds.
acceptance_criteria: A deploy whose only change is the ticfac binaries rebuilds only the final layers, and the measured rebuild time is recorded
